nodes.title: Store the selection as one key
nodes.why: One nullable key models single selection: each click replaces it, so the previous cell loses cell--active with no clearing step, and null is the state the status line shows as Selected: none.
nodes.alternative: Keep a boolean per cell in a two-dimensional array, or a Set of selected keys.
nodes.tradeoff: One key cannot express multi-select, but two cells can never be active at once, a rule that a grid of booleans would have to enforce in every click handler.

nodes.title: Derive the row indexes from the size

anchor.snippet: readonly rows = computed(() => Array.from({ length: this.size() }, (_, index) => index));

nodes.why: The template loops over rows() for both rows and columns, so one index array drives the whole N by N grid, and the computed rebuilds it only when size changes.
nodes.alternative: Return a fresh array from a rows getter on every check, or store a two-dimensional array of cell objects that onSizeChange rebuilds.
nodes.tradeoff: Plain indexes carry no per-cell data, so color and active state are worked out per cell in the template; a grid of cell objects could hold them but would need rebuilding on each resize and click.

nodes.title: Apply the size on change, not on every key
nodes.why: The field binds (change), which fires on Enter, on blur and on the arrows, so typing 12 passes through 1 without resizing the board. Clamping on every input event turned that 1 into 2 and rewrote the field, so sizes 10 to 19 could not be typed.
nodes.alternative: Handle (input) and apply only whole numbers that are already inside 2 to 20, leaving other keystrokes alone.
nodes.tradeoff: A change waits for Enter or blur, so a typed size shows one step later; live updates on input redraw sooner but pass through boards nobody asked for, such as 2 by 2 on the way to 25.

nodes.title: Clamp the committed size to 2 through 20
nodes.why: The value loses its decimals, then the Math.min and Math.max pair keeps the board between 2 and 20 cells per side, so no typed value can render an empty grid or thousands of buttons. An empty or non-numeric field keeps the current size.
nodes.alternative: Rely on the input's min and max attributes, which limit the spinner arrows and form validity but not what a user types.
nodes.tradeoff: The attributes still help, since the spinner stops at the bounds and the field reports itself invalid, but only the clamp guarantees the size the grid renders.

nodes.title: Write the clamped size back into the field
nodes.why: [value]="size()" writes the field only when size() changes. Typing 30 on a 20 by 20 board clamps to the same 20, so without this line the field would keep showing 30 beside a 20 by 20 board.
nodes.alternative: Keep the typed text in its own signal bound to [value] and set it again after each change.
nodes.tradeoff: Writing the element is one line in the handler. A text signal keeps the template in charge of the field but has the same blind spot: setting it to the value it already holds changes nothing, so the typed 30 would stay.

nodes.title: Clear the selection on every resize
nodes.why: A key such as 7-7 has no cell on a 5 by 5 board, so onSizeChange sets selectedKey back to null when the size changes, and the status line returns to Selected: none.
nodes.alternative: Keep the key when its row and column still fit the new size, and clear it only when they fall outside the board.
nodes.tradeoff: Clearing on every resize is one line and never leaves a stale key, but it also drops a selection that would still fit; committing the size the board already has returns early and keeps the selection.

nodes.title: Read the selection inside a per-cell method
nodes.why: cellClass needs a row and a column, which a computed cannot take, so it stays a method. Its selectedKey() read runs while the template renders, so the OnPush view still updates the classes when the selection changes.
nodes.alternative: Build a computed grid of cell view models with ready-made class strings and read them in the template by row and column.
nodes.tradeoff: The method runs once per cell on each check, at most 400 short calls on a 20 by 20 board; a computed grid would cache the strings but rebuild all of them on every click anyway.
